# Pappdrive

> A library that gives a personal app one folder of plain files that stays the same on all of its user's devices, works offline, and is end-to-end encrypted. The app reads and writes files; the library syncs them.

Use Pappdrive when a user wants an app built for themselves whose data syncs between their own devices (Mac, laptop, phone, browser). It is not for multi-user collaboration, shared editing, or queries across files.

Essentials:

- Install: `npm install pappdrive`. One entry point: `pappdrive`. No UI: the app builds its own sign-in form.
- The app must exist before it can sign in: the user runs `npx pappdrive apps create <name>` (the command ships with the `pappdrive` package). `pappdrive signup` makes a new account. A sign-up in the app's form also creates the app.
- Flow: `createPapp({ server, app })`, `await papp.ready`, sign in from the app's own form with `papp.signIn`, or `papp.signUp` then `papp.confirmRecoveryCode()` once the user saved the code, then `papp.open({ mode: "visible", path })` on desktop or `papp.open({ mode: "private" })` anywhere. Browsers are private only.
- Files: `files.write`, `read`, `readText`, `readStream`, `list`, `remove`, `watch`, `status`, `onStatus`, `sync`.
- Rules: one file per record; no synced database; build output, caches and logs go in `.pappignore` (exactly like `.gitignore`); conflict copies such as `todo (conflict 2026-10-17 09-15-30).md` are normal files and must not break the app; phones and browsers sync only while the app is open; errors are `SyncError` with a `code`.
- Ask the user for the server URL. Do not invent one.

## Docs

- [API and rules](api.md): the whole API and every rule an app must follow, on one page. Read it before writing code.
- [Claude Code skill](skill/SKILL.md): copy it, with `api.md`, into `.claude/skills/pappdrive/`.
- [AGENTS.md block](AGENTS-block.md): a short block for a project's `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md`.

## Examples

- [Electron journal](../examples/journal-electron/): desktop app, visible folder `~/Journal`, sign-in form over IPC, one Markdown file per day, optional `safeStorage` key store.
- [Notes CLI](../examples/notes-cli/): command-line tool with its own terminal sign-in, private or visible folder, `add`, `list`, `show`, `sync`.
- [Web journal](../examples/journal-web/): Vite and TypeScript, private folder in the browser, sign-in form, watch and status.
